paper.title: RoboPhD: Self-Improving Text-to-SQL Through Autonomous Agent Evolution
paper.central_claim: Autonomous cross-pollination with ELO selection evolves complete text-to-SQL tools and instructions without author-supplied domain expertise, improving unseen-database accuracy and enabling cheaper-model deployment.

provenance.notes: Configured execution identity gpt-6.1-sol supplied by dispatch; no independently exposed model receipt/session identifier. No model probing.

sections_read: Appendices A–E including prompts and naive code as data

evidence.quote: The evolved agent consists entirely of a Python script and a markdown file containing SQL generation instructions
evidence.support_explanation: Retained non-weight code and prompt artifacts.

evidence.quote: At runtime, answering a user’s question requires only this system prompt, the question, and any provided evidence
evidence.support_explanation: Later use does not require the evolutionary scaffold.

evidence.quote: It receives ELO rankings, accuracy metrics, and detailed error analysis
The evolution process is guided by a hand-crafted strategy prompt; evolving these strategies themselves is future work
evidence.support_explanation: Improver strategy is fixed; no improver-level result.

evidence.quote: After each testing round, the Evolution AI can refine its artifacts based on this performance feedback.
evidence.support_explanation: Deep Focus refinement is a selection/training operation, not a held-out test.

evidence.quote: The system evaluates three agents simultaneously on identical sets of databases and questions, computing overall accuracy using BIRD’s set-based comparison (row order ignored, exact match required).
evidence.support_explanation: Benchmark execution fitness and paired-task comparisons.

evidence.quote: (1) the previous winner, (2) the newly evolved agent, and (3) a random agent selected from the top 2 performers by ELO (other than the winner).
each iteration evaluates agents on only 5 randomly selected databases from the 69-database training set, with 30 randomly sampled questions per database
evidence.support_explanation: 150 selection questions per iteration; resampling is not independent reporting.

evidence.quote: Each evolution iteration (using only Haiku 4.5 LLMs for SQL generation) costs approximately $2 in Claude API for the calls and runs for 22 minutes on average
evidence.support_explanation: Search API/time costs reported, but proposer cost uses subscription quota.

evidence.quote: each 30-iteration run uses about 12% of the weekly usage quota of a Claude Max plan.
evidence.support_explanation: Quota disclosure is not a fully monetary/token-budget-matched comparison.

evidence.quote: The naive agent represents the starting point of our evolutionary process as well as our experimental baseline.
evidence.support_explanation: No matched alternative search/strong manually engineered control is reported.

evidence.quote: the evolved Opus agent improves by 2.3 points over naive Opus, the evolved Haiku agent gains 8.9 points
evidence.support_explanation: Cross-model gains of frozen evolved package on BIRD dev; no independent repeated-search variance.

evidence.quote: Evolution improves overall accuracy by 1.51 points (73.67% vs 72.16%)
evidence.support_explanation: Official test gain versus unchanged naive control.
Simple questions regress 81.35 to 81.03; challenging improves 48.42 to 55.44.

evidence.quote: were generated by the BIRD benchmark team using two configurations submitted by the authors.
evidence.support_explanation: External private test execution author-reported; no private test access by evolver claimed.

evidence.quote: The strategy requires deterministic Python tools rather than LLM-based analysis, ensuring speed and reproducibility.
evidence.support_explanation: Human-imposed tool-only design constrains autonomy and architecture scope.

evidence.quote: Self-Directed Improvement without Author-Supplied Domain Expertise
evidence.support_explanation: Original broad autonomy claim preserved, not silently narrowed.

evidence.quote: The key design innovation was a size-based feature matrix that adjusts analysis depth based on database complexity
evidence.support_explanation: Concrete reusable context-size repair, not independently ablated.

gap.author_gap: Prompt optimizers leave database-analysis code fixed; autonomous agent evolution needs selection despite changing sampled task difficulty.
gap.checked_gap: Whole tool plus instruction evolution is concrete; search novelty and elimination of human domain design are only partially substantiated.
closest_adjacent: TextGrad/ACE diagnostic editing; ELO-ranked program/prompt evolution; originals requested
gap.residue: whether ELO and tool cross-pollination improve quality per search dollar beyond simpler optimizer and a stronger starting tool
gap.stakes: reduce manual SQL agent engineering and deployment cost
gap.method_response: persistent program/prompt population, same-task comparisons, diagnostic mutation and historical challengers
gap.remaining_gap: No isolated search-mechanism comparison or non-SQL transfer; autonomy bounded by fixed strategy.
unresolved: Original APE/OPRO/DSPy/TextGrad/ACE and earliest ELO-guided program/prompt evolution sources are outside fixed material; first-use novelty not independently verified.

claims.text: Evolved complete agent packages improve unseen-database SQL accuracy.
claims.setting: BIRD dev three frozen model tiers and official Opus test
claims.baseline_control: naive raw-DDL 50-line tool plus minimal instructions; same model tier
claims.selection_vs_test: train sampling/Deep Focus selection; dev reporting and external private test separate
claims.result_denominator: dev Opus 69.0→71.3, Sonnet65.7→69.2, Haiku57.2→66.1; official Opus72.16→73.67; no reported CIs/repeated campaigns
claims.counterevidence: Simple private-test subset decreases 81.35→81.03; no strong alternative optimizer.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported retained non-weight package benefit on BIRD, not generic autonomous research or improver improvement.

claims.text: Evolution enables higher accuracy at lower cost.
claims.baseline_control: evolved Haiku vs naive Sonnet; evolved Sonnet vs naive Opus
claims.selection_vs_test: one-time training search versus subsequent inference
claims.result_denominator: 66.1%/.51 cents vs65.7%/.56 cents;69.2%/.87 cents vs69.0%/1.61 cents per query (Table1)
claims.counterevidence: Same-tier cost increases; search/proposer amortization not fully priced.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Specific deployment cross-tier tradeoffs only, not budget-matched search superiority.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported persistent code/prompt packages improve BIRD dev and official unseen-DB test over a minimal starting package; fixed evolution strategy and narrow benchmark limit autonomy/generalization.
unresolved: No original-neighbor novelty verification, independent execution reproduction, alternative improver comparison, or repeated-search uncertainty.

G.reason: Concrete bottleneck is manually fixed database analysis and instructions, beyond prompt wording alone. Prior APE/OPRO/DSPy/TextGrad/ACE discussed, but ELO-first and domain-expertise novelty not established by neighbor originals or strong controls.

M.reason: Code/instruction genome, same-task fitness, persistent ELO archive, parent selection and diagnostic refinement form a reconstructable response to fixed tool design. Scalar ELO does not establish nontransitive modeling; necessity of each component remains an untested hypothesis.

X.reason: Actual artifact files, fixed tool-only interface, historical parent reuse and deployable runtime are explicit. Broad archive selection is not a scoped monotone commit/rollback gate and several strategy/schedule choices are hand-authored.

E.measurement.reason: BIRD standard exact execution-result set equivalence and identical questions across competitors directly measure text-to-SQL execution success; externally executed test supports measurement credibility. This does not prove all-query semantic correctness.

E.causality.reason: Naive-versus-evolved package has controlled model tiers and retained-package gains, but naive is intentionally minimal; no budget-matched random/greedy/alternative optimizer, ELO removal, Deep Focus removal, or tool-versus-instructions ablation isolates proposed search mechanism.
search_scope: Full §§3–5, Appendices A–E; no controlled optimizer/component ablation table.

E.holdout.reason: Evolution uses training databases; author reports no private-test access and external test team evaluates two submitted configurations. Supports retained package on unseen DBs, not generic transfer or improver improvement. Pretraining contamination and champion/dev selection audit remain unreported.

E.statistics.reason: Training sample counts and negative simple-subset result are reported. Full paper including Appendix B reports API nondeterminism but no CIs, significance or repeated independent evolution campaigns; A2 ladder 1.
search_scope: Full §4 tables/analysis and Appendices A–E, especially reproducibility Appendix B; no uncertainty or across-search seeds.

E.cost.reason: Per-query model-tier cost table, $2/22min iterations, hardware and subscription quota are disclosed. Same-tier inference gets more costly; proposer quota, failed campaigns and search selection are not fully normalized or matched against other optimizers.

reason: Full pinned text and appendices read; retained non-weight code/prompt object and independent test result are in scope under A3. Evidence limitations rated, not treated as missing material.
rationale: 留存代码与指令在新数据库有增益，官方测试支持 retained；但弱起点、无搜索/组件消融、单次进化与固定人工策略限制因果及自主性主张。
